title: Matrices: Order, Addition and Multiplication
seo_title: Sec 4 Matrices Worksheets: Free Secondary 4 Maths with Answers (MOE Syllabus)
standard_text: display of information in the form of a matrix of any order; interpreting the data in a given matrix; product of a scalar quantity and a matrix; problems involving addition, subtraction and multiplication of matrices
meta_desc: Free Secondary 4 maths worksheets on matrices: displaying information, order of a matrix, addition, subtraction, scalar multiples, matrix multiplication and real-world problems. 100 questions with answers.
key_big: Multiply row by column; AB needs columns of A = rows of B.
key_sub: Add and subtract only matrices of the same order, entry by entry.
body_html:
How it works

  • A matrix with m rows and n columns has order m × n.
  • Add or subtract matrices of the same order entry by entry. A scalar multiplies every entry.
  • AB is defined only when the number of columns of A equals the number of rows of B. An m × n matrix times an n × p matrix gives an m × p matrix.
  • Each entry of AB is a row of A times a column of B: multiply matching entries and add.
Example

Find 123456.

Row 1: 1 × 5 + 2 × 6 = 17

Row 2: 3 × 5 + 4 × 6 = 39

Answer: 1739

Example

A is 2 × 3 and B is 3 × 1. What is the order of AB?

Inside numbers 3 and 3 match

Outside numbers give the order

Answer: 2 × 1

Common mistakes

  • Multiplying matrices entry by entry instead of row by column.
  • Writing the order as columns × rows.
  • Adding matrices of different orders.
  • Thinking AB = BA. Matrix multiplication usually depends on the order.

faq.q: What is the order of a matrix?
faq.a: The number of rows × the number of columns. A matrix with 2 rows and 3 columns has order 2 × 3.

faq.q: When can two matrices be multiplied?
faq.a: AB is defined when the number of columns in A equals the number of rows in B.

faq.q: How do you multiply two matrices?
faq.a: For each entry, take a row of the first matrix and a column of the second, multiply matching entries and add the results.

faq.q: What does a matrix product mean in a word problem?
faq.a: Multiplying a quantity matrix by a price matrix gives total costs: each row of quantities is multiplied by the prices and added.

sets.title: Order and when products are defined

items.q: A is 3 × 3 and B is 3 × 1. Is BA defined?
c: No, because B has 1 column but A has 3 rows
items.e: For BA, the columns of B (1) must equal the rows of A (3). No, because B has 1 column but A has 3 rows.

items.q: A is 2 × 3 and B is 3 × 3. Is BA defined?
c: No, because B has 3 columns but A has 2 rows
items.e: For BA, the columns of B (3) must equal the rows of A (2). No, because B has 3 columns but A has 2 rows.

items.q: A is 2 × 3 and B is 3 × 5. What is the order of AB?
items.e: The inside numbers match (3 = 3), so the product is defined. Its size is the outside numbers: 2 × 5.

items.q: A is 1 × 4 and B is 4 × 2. Is BA defined?

items.e: For BA, the columns of B (2) must equal the rows of A (1). No, because B has 2 columns but A has 1 row.
